# Loading models

## Overview

The `ems_model()` function loads the model and its closure, conducts pre-deployment checks, determines temporal dynamics, and allows for the loading of aggregated coefficient data.
The output of this function is a tibble with attributes containing the parsed model input and is a required input to the `"model"` argument of the [`ems_deploy()`](deploy.qmd) function.

```r
ems_model(
  model_file,
  closure_file,
  backsolve = NULL,
  ignore_condense = FALSE,
  ...
)
```

| Argument | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `model_file` | Character | File name in working directory or path to a `.tab` file |
| `closure_file` | Character | File name in working directory or path to a `.cls` closure file |
| `backsolve` | Character vector or `NULL` | Endogenous variables to substitute out by backsolving |
| `ignore_condense` | Logical | Ignore `Substitute`/`Backsolve` statements found in the model file |
| `...` | Named arguments | Coefficient value injections (numeric, data frame, or CSV path) |

Both `model_file` and `closure_file` are required arguments.

## The model file {#tab_files}

Model input in `teems` is limited to Tablo (`.tab`) files.
Vetted models and their closures are available at [teems-models](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-models) and through [`ems_example()`](example.qmd):

| Model | Description | Database |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| GTAPv6 | Classic GTAP model, version 6.2 | GTAP v6.2 format |
| GTAPv7 | Standard GTAP model, version 7.1 | GTAP v7 format |
| GTAP-RE | GTAP with rational expectations (intertemporal) | GTAP v7 format |
| GTAP-AEZ | GTAP with land use by agro-ecological zone | GTAP-AEZ release |
| GTAP-E | GTAP with energy substitution and carbon taxes | GTAP-E release |
| GTAP-EP | GTAP-E with the electricity sector split by generation technology | GTAP-Power release |
| ORANI-G | Single-country model of the Centre of Policy Studies, 2013 edition | Its own `basedata.har` |

Users may load their own models by providing a path to a Tablo file and closure:
```r
model <- ems_model(
  model_file = "path/to/custom_model.tab",
  closure_file = "path/to/custom_model.cls"
)
```

When preparing a custom model, the vetted models are a good reference, and often the easiest starting point for modifications.

## Closure selection
Standard model-specific closures are available within the model repository: [teems-models](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-models).
The general format consists of an `exogenous` block listing all (`\n` delimited) exogenous variables, followed by `;`, `rest endogenous`, and `;` to mark the end:

```
exogenous
pop
aoreg("row")
qe(ENDWC,REG,INITIME)
txs(MARG,"row",REG,FWDTIME)
...
;
rest endogenous
;
```

Each entry is either a full variable name (`pop`), an entry with specific set elements (`aoreg("row")`), an entry with subsets (`qe(ENDWC,REG,INITIME)`) or a mixed entry (`txs(MARG,"chn",REG,FWDTIME)`).

## Tablo compatibility

The [teems-solver](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems-solver) follows GEMPACK's Tablo language, so most model files written for GEMPACK load as they are.
This manual will not attempt to reproduce the very thorough [GEMPACK documentation](https://www.copsmodels.com/gpmanual.htm), rather lists what is supported and the few forms that are not.
`ems_model()` checks the model file before anything is solved.
Problems are reported by name, with the statement it occurs in, rather than surfacing later as a solver failure.
If a model file does not load and you think it should, a supported statement behavior is not as expected, or an error propagates to the solver without warning, please [get in touch](https://github.com/teemsphere/teems/issues).

### Supported statements

`File`, `Coefficient`, `Read`, `Update`, `Set`, `Subset`, `Mapping`, `Formula`, `Assertion`, `Variable`, `Equation`, `Write`, `Zerodivide`, `Complementarity`, `PostSim` sections, and the condensation statements `Substitute` and `Backsolve` (see [Condensation](#condensation)) are accepted.
`Omit` statements hold the omitted variables exogenous and unshocked, as omission does in GEMPACK; they stay in the model and its outputs.
Levels variables and equations, `Formula & Equation`, and `Read (IfHeaderExists)` are supported; levels equations may contain conditional sums and the functions `SQRT`, `EXP`, `LOGE` and `LOG10`.
`Default` statements (`Variable (Default=Levels);`, `Equation (Default=Levels);`, `Formula (Default=Initial);`, `Coefficient (Default=Parameter);`) apply to the statements that follow them, as in GEMPACK.
In closures, shocks and swaps a levels variable may also be named by its linear variable, `c_X` for a `(change)` variable and `p_X` otherwise.
A coefficient may itself be named `C_X` as long as no variable `X` exists.

`Loop`, `Display`, `Break`, `Cycle` and `Transfer` are not supported and raise an error.

### Names

Names are case-insensitive, as in GEMPACK.
A set, coefficient, variable, file or equation may be written in any case after its declaration, and TEEMS uses the declared spelling throughout, including in outputs.
The same holds for header names (`Read ... header "Nat"` finds a header `NAT`), logical file names, the `.tab` and `.har` extensions, and the variable, set and element names in closures, shocks and swaps.

### Formulas, updates and mappings

- `Formula` quantifiers may carry general conditions, such as `(all,c,COM: $POS(c) = $POS(g))`, a coefficient on either side, or a mapping (`MAP(z) = r`).
  `Update` statements take quantifier conditions too; an element whose condition is false is left unchanged.
- A qualifier list such as `(initial, by_elements)` is accepted.
  `write updated value to file` is accepted with a warning but writes no separate file; the value is in the coefficient outputs.
- An index may be repeated within one reference (`T(d,d)`, `TRADE(c,"dom",r,r)`).
- A mapping may point into a subset of the set its argument position is declared over, and a mapped index may range over a subset of the mapping's domain.
  A mapping may also be assigned an identity or a copy (`MAP(c) = c`, `A(z) = B(z)`).
- `Update` statements read the values at the start of each step, and several updates of one element apply in order, the later overriding, as in GEMPACK.
  `(change)` and `(explicit)` updated data follow the solution path and are extrapolated like the variables; see [single-pass runs](solve.qmd#single-pass) for models where that is not wanted.

### Sets

Sets may be read from file, listed explicitly, or built from other sets:

```
Set A123 = A1 + A2 + A3;
Set B = (C - D) INTERSECT E;
Set B2 # equal to A # = A;
Set UACT = UNITA x ACTS;
Set COALCOMM # coal # = (all,c,COMM: sum{cc,DCOMM: MCOM(cc)=c, UNITDCOAL(cc)} > 0);
```

Set expressions (`UNION`, `INTERSECT`, `+`, `-`), set equality, set products and conditional set builders all follow GEMPACK.
A few points to note:

- Set names must not contain the substrings `union` or `intersect`.
- A conditional set builder, like `COALCOMM` above, compares an expression with a constant.
  Its source set may be read, listed or itself built from other sets.
  Sets are built before formulas are calculated, so the coefficients in the condition must be read from a file or assigned constants only, as GTAP-E's `UNITDCOAL(c) = 0.0 + IF[c="coa", 1.0]` is.
- The upstream GTAP models build some sets from the `EFLG` and `SLUG` headers, which TEEMS excludes from the data.
  Declare such sets with explicit elements instead.
- Intertemporal set equality (`Set (Intertemporal) B = A;`) is not supported.
- A set may be empty, for example when a conditional set builder selects nothing under the data at hand.
  Statements over an empty set do nothing and sums over it are zero.

Set element names are lowercase throughout TEEMS (see [Set mappings](set_mappings.qmd)); for example, the v6.2 `CGDS` sector becomes `cgds`.

Element order follows the data file wherever a set is not aggregated (see [Loading data](data_load.qmd)).
It matters to anything that works by position, such as `$POS` and a mapping read from a header, whose entries line up with the elements of its domain in order.

### IF conditions

`IF[condition, expression]` terms are supported in formulas and equations when they are added at the top level of an expression:

```
Formula (all,c,COMM)(all,r,REG)
    VCB(c,r) = VDB(c,r) + sum{d,REG, VXSB(c,r,d)} + IF[c in MARG, VST(c,r)];
Equation E_qca (all,c,COMM)(all,a,ACTS)(all,r,REG)
    qca(c,a,r) = IF[MAKES(c,a,r) gt 0, qo(a,r) - ETRAQ(a,r) * [ps(c,a,r) - po(a,r)]];
```

A condition may test set membership (`c in MARG`), compare an index with an element or another index (`d = "domestic"`, `r <> s`), or compare coefficient expressions (`MAKES(c,a,r) gt 0`).
`IF` terms may be nested inside one another, and may appear in formulas without quantifiers (`Formula D = 0.0 + IF[NM > 1, 1];`).
At model load they are rewritten into equivalent unconditional statements; helper coefficients and sets created this way (named `IFC*`, `IFX*`, `IFT*`, `IFV*`, `IFO*`) appear in outputs like any other coefficient or set.

Not supported: compound conditions (`AND`, `OR`, `NOT`), `IF` inside sums or products, and conditions on different indices at the same level of one equation.

## Condensation {#condensation}

Condensation makes the system passed to the solver smaller without changing the model's economics.
TEEMS condenses by backsolving variables.

**The five static vetted models come condensed.**
Their model files carry the standard GTAP backsolves as `Backsolve` statements, which `ems_model()` applies on load.
GTAP-RE carries none, because backsolving slows the parallel methods intertemporal models use (see [below](#backsolve_when)).
To solve the full system, load a model with `ignore_condense = TRUE`.

### Backsolving variables {#backsolve}

A backsolved variable is substituted out of the system using its defining equation and recovered by the solver after each step, so it still appears in the outputs.
By default the defining equation is `E_<variable>`; name it explicitly when it differs:

```r
model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAPv7[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAPv7[["closure_file"]],
  backsolve = c("pfd", "pfm", ps = "E_ps")
)
```

A backsolved variable must be endogenous, and its defining equation must be one GEMPACK could substitute with.
If it is not, the error names the requirement that failed.
Coefficients created along the way (named `CSUB*`) appear in outputs like any other coefficient.

### When backsolving pays {#backsolve_when}

Backsolving shrinks the system but makes it denser.
That helps `"LU"` on static models, and hurts the parallel matrix methods (`"SBBD"`, `"DBBD"`, `"NDBBD"`), which rely on the sparsity it removes.
[`ems_probe()`](solve.qmd#recommended) takes this into account when it recommends a method.

### Condensation statements in the model file

`Substitute` and `Backsolve` statements in a model file are applied on load:

```
Substitute p1 using E_p1 ;
Backsolve p1lab using E_p1lab ;
```

`Substitute` is carried out as a backsolve, so the variable stays in the outputs.
Statements in the file are applied first, then the `backsolve` argument.
`ignore_condense = TRUE` skips the statements in the file but still applies the argument.

`Omit` statements add the listed variables to the closure as exogenous, unshocked entries, with a message.
They stay in the model and its outputs, so a closure file need not repeat them.

Closure files may also carry `xSet` and `xSubset` lines as written in a GEMPACK command file; they are read as `Set` and `Subset` statements of the model, so closure entries can refer to them.

## Coefficient value injection {#coeff_inject}

The `...` argument in `ems_model()` allows users to assign aggregation-specific values to model coefficients.
This is used to inject modified values into existing coefficients as well as provide data to new coefficients.
All data inputted here must be model-aggregation specific and will not be subject to aggregation.
The left-hand side (name) must correspond to a coefficient (not header) declared within the model input.
Data frame and CSV inputs are validated against the set aggregations from [`ems_data()`](data_load.qmd).
Dimensions must match the aggregated resolution, not the original database resolution.
Three input types are supported, with model "Read" and "Formula" declarations modified accordingly:

### Uniform numeric value

A single numeric value can be assigned to a coefficient.
All set combinations for that coefficient will receive this uniform value.

```r
GTAP_RE <- ems_example("GTAP-RE")
model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAP_RE[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAP_RE[["closure_file"]],
  KAPPA = 0.54321
)
```

Providing a numeric vector of length greater than 1 will raise an error.
Instead here use a data frame with the appropriate sets to assign multiple heterogeneous values to a coefficient.

### Data frame

A data frame (or data frame extension such as tibble or data.table) can be used to assign heterogeneous values across set combinations.
The data frame must contain columns for each set index using the model-specific naming convention (set name + variable index, e.g., `REGr`, `COMMc`, `ALLTIMEt`) and a `Value` column.

```r
# Heterogeneous values for SUBPAR coefficient (Read-type)
GTAP_RE <- ems_example("GTAP-RE")
COMMc <- c("crops", "food", "livestock", "mnfcs", "svces")
REGr <- c("usa", "chn", "row")
ALLTIMEt <- seq(0, 10)

SUBPAR <- expand.grid(
  COMMc = COMMc,
  REGr = REGr,
  ALLTIMEt = ALLTIMEt
)

SUBPAR$Value <- runif(nrow(SUBPAR))

model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAP_RE[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAP_RE[["closure_file"]],
  SUBPAR = SUBPAR
)
```

This works for both `Read`-type and `Formula`-type coefficients:

```r
# Heterogeneous values for CPHI coefficient (Formula-type)
REGr <- c("usa", "chn", "row")
ALLTIMEt <- seq(0, 10)

CPHI <- expand.grid(
  REGr = REGr,
  ALLTIMEt = ALLTIMEt
)
CPHI$Value <- runif(nrow(CPHI))

model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAP_RE[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAP_RE[["closure_file"]],
  CPHI = CPHI
)
```

### CSV file

A path to a CSV file can be used as an alternative to a data frame.
The CSV must follow the same structure: set index columns and a `Value` column.

```r
# Write coefficient data to CSV
write.csv(SUBPAR, "SUBPAR.csv", row.names = FALSE)

model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAP_RE[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAP_RE[["closure_file"]],
  SUBPAR = "SUBPAR.csv"
)
```

### Combining injections

Multiple coefficient injections can be combined in a single call:

```r
model <- ems_model(
  model_file = GTAP_RE[["model_file"]],
  closure_file = GTAP_RE[["closure_file"]],
  KAPPA = 0.03,
  SUBPAR = SUBPAR,
  CPHI = CPHI
)
```

If the coefficient name is not found in the model, an error is raised indicating that the aggregated data coefficient is not declared within the provided model input.

## Intertemporal models {#intertemporal}

For intertemporal models, `ems_model()` determines temporal dynamics by detecting intertemporal sets in the Tablo file.
By default, the expected header in the GTAP-RE model is `"YEAR"`.
If a model uses a different header for timestep data, set it via [`ems_option_set()`](options.qmd):

```r
ems_option_set(timestep_header = "AYRS")
```

If the expected timestep header is not found in the model, an error will be raised with a suggestion to use [`ems_option_set()`](options.qmd) to configure a custom timestep header.
The same concept applies to the number of timesteps:

```r
ems_option_set(n_timestep_header = "NINTERVAL")
```

Default values for these settings (and others) may be obtained using:

```r
ems_option_get()
```

### Leads, lags and parallel solving {#netcut}
(check this passage)
In intertemporal models, the parallel matrix methods (see [Solving the model](solve.qmd)) solve each period as a block, with the variables that link periods held in a shared border.
A lead or lag on a variable declared over large sets (for example `qo(c,r,t+1)` over all commodities and regions) enlarges that border and can remove the benefit of solving in parallel.

Link periods through a small proxy variable instead:

``` default
Variable (all,r,REG)(all,t,ALLTIME)
    kb(r,t) # beginning-of-period capital stock #;
Equation E_kb
(all,r,REG)(all,t,ALLTIME)
    kb(r,t) = qo("capital",r,t);
```

and place the lead on the proxy (`kb(r,t+1)`).
`ems_model()` does this automatically when a lead or lag fixes some dimensions to elements (`qo("capital",r,t+1)`), and warns when it cannot.
The vetted intertemporal models already follow this pattern.
